question: Many dishwasher tablets come in a thin, plastic-looking wrapper, and the box tells you not to unwrap them. Why is it safe to throw them in wrapper and all?
source_excerpt: dishwashing components are packed into a water-soluble film of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)

extra.why_interesting: Wrapping that looks like plastic packaging instinctively gets torn off, so being told to leave it on feels wrong. Realising it simply melts away in water is a small 'oh, of course' moment the player can reason toward.
extra.verification_notes: Dishwasher tablet film is water-soluble PVA that dissolves in wash water, per the EPO examination report at https://link.epo.org/elearning/Paper_A_2017_EN.pdf.

explanation: The film is polyvinyl alcohol, a water-soluble material that disappears in the wash. It also keeps your fingers from touching the strong detergent inside.
